result.summary: Fix a memory leak when spawning subprocesses on Windows by passing `std::string::data()` directly to `CreateProcessA` instead of heap-allocating a copy. This eliminates an undeleted `new[]` buffer allocation in `Popen::execute_process()`.
result.problem: On Windows, `Popen::execute_process()` allocates a command-line buffer on the heap using `new[]` but never deletes it, leaking memory every time a subprocess starts. In Bitcoin Core, this affects Windows nodes configured with `-signer=<cmd>` whenever an external signer process is invoked.
evidence: PR description and commit: "Popen::execute_process() copied the command line into a buffer from new[], but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows."

PR description: "This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if -signer=<cmd> is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined <cmd>, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited."
result.card: Fixes a memory leak in Windows subprocess execution where Popen::execute_process() allocated a command line buffer using new[] without deleting it. The fix passes std::string::data() directly to CreateProcessA, removing the temporary allocation entirely. The leak affects Windows nodes configured with an external signer (-signer=<cmd>) on each signer invocation, though impact is limited by the invocation rate and small command size.

risk.why: A flaw in the buffer passed to CreateProcessA would fail external signer subprocess invocations on Windows.
